races.title: State House, District 119
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Anna Ferguson
cands.bio: Anna Ferguson is a Republican who was appointed to the North Carolina House, District 119, in April 2026 after Mike Clampitt's death. A member of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, she is a longtime business owner with experience in construction finance, and she attended N.C. State.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birth year or the year her business began. The pages we had contain no stated positions from her on data centers, development and growth, property taxes, housing purchases by investors or out-of-state buyers, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. We found no record of actions she took in office; the list of bills she sponsored on her Ballotpedia page was empty. We found no endorsements. We did not read any news coverage of her appointment, so the details of how she was chosen are limited to a brief Wikipedia statement and Ballotpedia's note that the governor appointed her.

local.label: Roots 100: Ferguson says she was born and raised in the Qualla Community and is the third generation to live on her family farm; the district she ran in includes the Qualla Boundary.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Business owner and president for over 30 years, with a career in construction finance. She held the District 119 House seat by appointment from April 16, 2026, to January 2027. She also served on the EBCI audit and ethics board and the Cherokee Planning Board.
qual.why: Running a business for decades and a short stretch in the House place her in the middle range. Her board and planning-board seats are not counted, and she has no long record in law, policy or budget work.
qual.label: Running a business for decades and a short stretch in the House place her in the middle range. Her board and planning-board seats are not counted, and she has no long record in law, policy or budget work.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said she will prioritize competitive teacher pay and increased public school funding. She did not state a position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

cands.name: Mark Burrows
cands.bio: Mark Burrows of Brevard is a Democrat who won the NC House District 119 seat in 2026. He has worked 30+ years in Transylvania County local government on economic development and planning. He is a certified planner (AICP) with a Duke master's degree. He lost the 2024 race for this seat.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club, as listed by the candidate in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey.
Voter-guide recommendations from the Sway groups Fair Map Fight Club, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Burrows was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We know only that he has lived in Brevard since about 1990. We could not confirm his exact job titles in county government or his employment dates. He has held no elected office, so there is no legislative record. We found no votes, bills or official actions to show what he has done on any of the issues voters care about, only what he has said. One report says he opposed a proposed constitutional amendment on local property tax rates, but we found no detail on it and left it out. We found nothing on his positions on guns, immigration, policing or growth limits.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Over 30 years in Transylvania County local government on economic development, planning and community development, including fiscal policy analysis and long-range planning. He has no prior legislative or elected office on record.
qual.why: Long local-government planning, economic development and fiscal policy work places him in the middle band. There is no legislative service or chamber leadership, and board and committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: Long local-government planning, economic development and fiscal policy work places him in the middle band. There is no legislative service or chamber leadership, and board and committee seats were not counted.

stop-data-centers.evidence: He said in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey that he does not support data centers in the community because they would raise utility rates and harm the environment, and that he wants to keep them out of Western North Carolina.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he listed protecting women's reproductive rights and health care privacy as a key campaign message.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: "I do not support data centers in our community which will raise utility rates and harm the environment." He also listed keeping data centers out of Western North Carolina as a policy priority.
